attempts.note: The previous attempt named no dataset (reason given: I found no public dataset that holds troglobitic species from both North America and Europe together with their nearest-relative or phylogenetic placement, so I could not name one I had fetched. The nearest candidate I fetched was the Biodiversity Data Journal data paper 'Continental data on cave-dwelling spider communities across Europe (Arachnida: Araneae)' (https://bdj.pensoft.net/article/38492/). It covers Europe only, so it cannot test the America-versus-Europe comparison the claim needs, and I did not use it. The other regional sets I came across were the Tennessee troglobiont database, which is American only and has no dataset DOI, and the USGS Appalachian karst grids, which are American only. I did not fetch either. A GBIF occurrence search cannot isolate troglobites, because GBIF has no cave-obligate flag. Without a curated cave-species list, the claim cannot be tested from GBIF. Naming GBIF, or a single-continent dataset, would be a weakened version of the claim, so I am returning null.).

The previous attempt named no dataset (reason given: I found no public dataset that I could fetch and that holds cave-obligate species from both America and Europe together with their phylogenetic placement or nearest relatives. The nearest candidate was the Dryad dataset 'Data from: Phylogenomics and biogeography of North American Trechine cave beetles (Coleoptera: Carabidae)' (DOI 10.5061/dryad.sj3tx967w). The European spider data paper (https://bdj.pensoft.net/article/38492/) covers Europe only. Naming either would test a weakened version of the claim.).

The previous attempt named no dataset (reason given: I did not find a public dataset that holds metacarpal length and breadth for ox, sheep and giraffe together and that I could fetch and check. The candidates I searched for and read about were these. The Mendeley Data set "In search of draught cattle" covers cattle only. Ríos, Danowitz and Solounias (2016, Palaeontologia Electronica, doi 10.26879/653) cover giraffids only and I found no data file on the article page. Sheep metapodial measurements exist only as a thesis supplement for sheep. Specimen-level portals such as VertNet and iDigBio, and MorphoSource, may hold the needed measurements, but I did not locate and fetch a specific dataset record for all three taxa. Rather than name an unverified identifier, I set the dataset to null.).

The previous attempt named no dataset (reason given: Searches of Dryad (including its API), plus general web searches, turned up no public per-individual dataset of bovid horn measurements with separate left and right values. The Dryad hits were beetle horns, calf disbudding wound healing, and mule deer antlers, which are cervid antlers rather than hollow horns. The relevant bovid studies (Sanmartinero creole cattle, Catalan goats, Alpine ibex) have no data deposit that I could confirm. I did not name any identifier I could not fetch and verify.).

The previous attempt named no dataset (reason given: No suitable public per-individual dataset with separate left and right bovid horn measurements could be found and fetched. Searches of Dryad and the wider web returned only datasets that do not record per-side horn values. Examples are Tidière et al. 2020 on ontogenetic horn-length allometry, and a dataset on female horn investment that uses species-level maxima from Bovids of the World. The left-right asymmetry studies I found (Catalan goat horns, mouflon trophies, domestic sheep skull geometric morphometrics) appear as journal articles or institutional repository records. I could not confirm a downloadable raw data deposit for any of them. I opened no dataset landing page, and I name no identifier I did not verify.).
